2026 - 2027 I PY27 NH Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) Procedures Manual 6 2. INTRODUCTION

The NH Department of Energy (NH DOE) is responsible for the statewide administration of the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance block grant (LIHEAP) referred to as the Fuel Assistance Program (FAP). LIHEAP is federally funded through the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (US DHHS). The NH DOE in turn contracts with five, locally based Community Action Agencies (CAA) to provide services to eligible households.

The Fuel Assistance Program provides certified income-eligible households with assistance in paying their energy bills during the winter heating season. The NH program prioritizes households where elderly, disabled persons, and/or young children reside. Benefits are calculated by considering household income for all residents in the home, housing type/size, fuel type, and the energy costs for that housing type within a region. This targeting allows those households with the lowest income and the highest energy cost to receive the highest benefits.

Coordination between Fuel Assistance and Weatherization

The NH DOE is also responsible for the administration of the Weatherization Assistance Program (WAP), funded through the U.S. Department of Energy (US DOE). Therefore, every effort will be made to coordinate services between the Fuel Assistance Program and the Weatherization Assistance Program to provide the best possible benefits to those who require services from both programs.

The LIHEAP statute (Section 2605 (b) (1) (c)) allows LIHEAP funding for low-cost residential weatherization and other cost-effective energy-related repair. LIHEAP will allocate funding for LIHEAP Funded Weatherization measures to FAP-eligible households when funds allow.

The Fuel Assistance/Electric Assistance/Weatherization Assistance Application (Attachment A) is the form utilized for the New Hampshire Fuel Assistance, Electric Assistance, and Weatherization Programs.

The joint Fuel Assistance/Electric Assistance/Weatherization Assistance application was designed to allow a client who is applying for fuel assistance benefits to apply for electric assistance and weatherization services at the same time. By installing energy efficiency measures, clients may reduce their dependency on the Fuel Assistance Program or may have their fuel assistance benefits extend further into the heating season since clients served by the Weatherization Assistance Program have warmer, less drafty, and more energy-efficient homes.

2026 - 2027 I PY27 NH Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) Procedures Manual 7 3. GLOSSARY

Apartment: An individual dwelling containing a bathroom, kitchen, and separate entrance located within one exterior building that has two or more separate residential units

Application Date: The date entered on the application in ECOS. This date should be the date the application was received by the CAA via email, online application, mail, fax, or in person drop off. If the applicant completed an in-person or over the phone interview in lieu of an application, this is the date of in-person interview

APTD: Aid to the Permanently and Totally Disabled

Benefit: The certified dollar amount of assistance that a FAP-certified eligible household is qualified to receive

CAA: Community Action Agency

Certifier: An appointed CAA staff member familiar with the FAP’s qualification requirements who reviews the applications for completeness and accuracy and deems the applications eligible or ineligible for benefits based upon the information gathered from the applicants

Disabled: Physical or mental impairments which substantially limit one or more major life activities, which are compensated for with a disability payment such as SSDI, SSI, APTD, or VA disability for a long-term disability

ECOS: An acronym for Energy Community Online System, ECOS is the statewide software program that New Hampshire utilizes to administer the Fuel Assistance Program.

Elderly: Age sixty (60) years or older

Energy Emergency: A condition that poses a serious threat to the health and safety of the household due to the lack of home energy

FANF: Financial Assistance to Needy Families (formerly TANF)

Foster Care Payments: A reimbursement for the in-home care of the foster person that is not considered income to the household. The foster adult/child is not listed or counted as a household member on the application. Foster care payments must be documented and noted in the comments section of the application.

2026 - 2027 I PY27 NH Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) Procedures Manual 10 4. ANNUAL FUEL ASSISTANCE PROGRAM SCHEDULE

July

CAAs begin taking and certifying FAP applications for any household with a member who is age 60 or over, disabled, or a child under 6 years of age or a household who uses wood as their primary heating fuel source.

August CAAs continue processing priority applications

September Annual program meeting held with vendors and staff. September 30 is the end of the federal fiscal year/funding period.

October October is the start of the federal fiscal year and LIHEAP/FAP funding period. CAAs must submit start of year items including their annual budget, outreach plan and Assurance 16 plan by October 1. CAAs all officially begin taking and certifying FAP applications for all applicants, prioritizing households that heat with a deliverable fuel. Weatherization begins responding to no-heat emergencies.

November Preparation for the FAP season to open begins, including opening communication to vendors and a press release issued. Vendor and client notifications begin just before or after Thanksgiving.

December FAP opens after New Hampshire receives notification of the federal LIHEAP grant award, generally by December 1. The CAAs begin making vendor payments. Applications for households experiencing an energy emergency will be processed within 18 hours for life-threatening situations and within 48 hours for situations that are non- life- threatening.

January FAP Program and Fiscal Monitoring begin at the CAAs.

February Updated Federal Poverty Guidelines, released each January, will be programmed into system. Monitoring continues at the CAAs.

March Monitoring continues at the CAAs. Weatherization no-heat emergencies end on March 31.

April The deadline for households to apply for FAP is April 30 (or first weekday in May if on a weekend). Season closing communication sent to vendors.

2026 - 2027 I PY27 NH Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) Procedures Manual 12 5. THE APPLICATION PROCESS

Eligibility for the New Hampshire Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) is based upon the following requirements:

• The household’s primary residence is in New Hampshire • Household members occupy the residence at time of application and during heating season • The total household size – all residents who are members of that household • The total household’s total gross income • The household is responsible for energy costs, either directly or through rent payment

The New Hampshire definition of "household" is drawn directly from the Federal Low Income Home Energy Assistance Act, as amended. This definition provides two criteria which must be met to establish the presence of a "household":

• An individual or group of individuals living together as one "economic unit" who purchase energy in common

Categorical eligibility, where a person or household qualifies for one program simply because they are a participant in another program, shall not be utilized for the FAP. Any household wishing to participate in the program must complete an application and document eligibility based upon household income for all members.

The local CAA shall determine eligibility through the application and certification process. The CAA shall ensure that applicants have provided required and accurate documentation of gross income as indicated on the application for all household members and attest to the truth of the information submitted. It is the responsibility of the applicant to provide all required documentation to the CAA as part of the application process. All applications must be complete, with all supporting documentation attached. Proof of valid Social Security numbers (SSN) or appropriate documentation for qualified non-citizens are required for all household members listed on the FAP application. A copy of the documentation should be saved in the application. If an applicant does not want their SSN documentation stored, a staff member must review the documentation to verify it is valid, enter the number into ECOS, and then document this verification process in notes. Babies under 1 year of age may be entered as a household member without a Social Security number by selecting “No identification number’ in ECOS and listing the reason as child under 1 year of age. If this child appears on a future application above age 1, the correct SSN must be verified and entered at that time.

2026 - 2027 I PY27 NH Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) Procedures Manual 13 benefit year will be denied for previous assistance. If a person was previously included on an application that was awarded a benefit that year, they cannot be included in a second application that program year.

The New Hampshire Fuel Assistance Program procedures are intended to ensure that low- income households have access to services in a timely manner. During the program year of December 1 through the end of the program on/around April 30, an application should be started within 30 days. If an applicant chooses to complete their application in person, the applicant must have the opportunity to schedule an appointment within 30 days of the request.

Taking the Application

All required information must be recorded accurately on the FAP application, including the number of household members, dwelling data, income information, vendor name and account information and a dated signature from the applicant. Utility accounts should be verified annually, with accounts verified at least every other year for liquid fuel accounts (oil, kerosene, propane). The application can be submitted on paper, online via the ECOS system, via fax, email, or in-person as an interview. Regardless of the application method, it is the responsibility of the CAA to verify that this information is complete and correct.

Documenting Income

Applicants must provide documentation for all gross income for the household. This documentation may include benefit letters, payroll stubs, signed statements from the payment source, statements for pension or interest, and other documentation as deemed appropriate by the CAA. Use of bank statements as documentation of income must be approved via waiver by Department of Energy staff. For sources of earned or unearned income, please consult the lists that follow in this section. It is the responsibility of the CAA to ensure that all income documentation is accurate, legible, and complete and uploaded and saved properly into ECOS.

Income is calculated by adding all countable, gross income from every source for each household member listed on the FAP application. The countable income for all household members must be entered into ECOS, which will then create a total household income to determine household income eligibility. Income documented should reflect the current household income, most frequently the income during the month prior to application submission. If the household’s financial circumstances change during the application review process, the present month income can be used to establish eligibility.

2026 - 2027 I PY27 NH Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) Procedures Manual 14 Income can be entered in various frequencies, such as weekly, monthly, or annually, and the ECOS system will automatically add all income and annualize the amount. For example, if a person is paid weekly, the most recent four consecutive paychecks should have the gross amounts entered. If a household member receives a Social Security benefit once a month, the monthly gross amount should be entered. If someone receives a cash assistance benefit in the same amount twice each month, it should be entered as semimonthly. Some income sources should be listed annually, such as self-employment income, annuities, IRAs, commission, and seasonal or contracted employees, including educational employees (e.g., teachers or school administrators). Section 6 contains guidance on special income situations.

Expenses that are eligible as income deductions, such as Medicare deductions or child support paid, can be entered as an expense and will reduce the total income. Any income calculations not captured by the ECOS system should be documented in notes or on an uploaded file.

Documenting No or Low Income Households

Households with no or very low income must provide written documentation of how the household has met its basic living expenses such as rent, energy costs, and food. Household income is considered very low if the total is less than the amount needed for monthly rent or mortgage. Documentation may include a statement from town or city welfare, friends or family, a SNAP notification letter, or other assistance provided during the determination period.

2026 - 2027 I PY27 NH Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) Procedures Manual 17 Allowable Expenses (aka Income Disregards)

Child support (regular) payments paid out during the income period $50 of earned interest and/or dividends annually Medicare deductions from Social Security or Railroad Retirement benefits (Part B and Part D) Mileage Reimbursement from employer (if reflected in gross amount on pay stub)

Income Guidelines

At the time of the application, total household size and total income are needed to determine the appropriate income level under the FAP Income Guidelines (Attachment B). Income eligibility is divided into six levels based on the most recent Federal Poverty Guidelines (FPG):

A 75% FPG or less B 75.01-100% FPG C 100.01-125% FPG D 125.01-150%, FPG E 150.01-175% FPG F 175.01% FPG up to 60% State Median Income (SMI)

Level F eligibility may be decreased to 200% FPG if funds are limited during the program year.

Calculating the Number of Rooms

The total number of rooms in a residential dwelling is necessary to utilize the Heating Cost Formula (Attachment C) when calculating heating costs. Non-room spaces such as hallways, unfinished basements, garages, attics, closets, etc., are not counted in the total number of rooms.

The Heating Cost Tables are based upon Design Heat Load Calculations (DHLC) and each type of unit assumes a standard room size.

The standard room sizes are as follows:

Single Family House:

144 square feet

Apartment, Condo or Duplex:

120 square feet

Mobile Home:

100 square feet

When a room is larger than the standard room size, the square foot total may be relied upon to calculate the number of rooms for a residential dwelling.

2026 - 2027 I PY27 NH Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) Procedures Manual 18 Examples:

1. The kitchen/living rooms in a mobile home are located in one large room with no dividing wall. The approximate room dimensions (supplied by the applicant) are 14 feet by 10 feet or 140 square feet. This would count as TWO rooms, since it is more than the room size by the DHLC for mobile homes of 100 square feet.

2. The kitchen, living room and bedroom are all located in one room of a single-family house. The approximate room dimension is 270 square feet. This would count as TWO rooms, as it is more than the room size used for a single-family house of 144 square feet. However, it is only two rooms, not three, since it is less than twice the DHLC amount of 288 sq ft (144 x 2).

3. The dining room/living room combination is located in one room in an apartment. The approximate room dimensions 110 square feet. This would count as ONE room, since it is less than the room size used by the DHLC for apartments of 120 square feet.

Calculating Heating Costs

In addition to income, annual household heating costs are also used to determine eligibility for the FAP. Annual heating costs can be calculated two ways, either by using the household’s actual energy usage or by using the Heating Cost Estimate (Attachment C) that is updated annually. By entering information regarding the dwelling and fuel type, an estimated heating cost is established. The system will automatically use this amount in the benefit determination.

Actual heating costs can be used for households with high energy usage. Actual heating costs must include an annual amount and can be documented with receipts, bills, vendor printouts, or statements. Annual heating costs can be entered into ECOS on the Energy Billing Data Detail screen under the Vendor tab. You can enter the actual annual heating cost in the Billing box on this screen. To use this amount in the benefit determination, the person issuing the benefit will want to select the heating cost type titled “Client Reported” (instead of Design Heat Load). This will use the actual heating cost amount entered instead of the system estimated cost. You can review this determination and compare it to the Design Heat Load determination to see which yields the best benefit for the applicant.

2026 - 2027 I PY27 NH Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) Procedures Manual 19 Calculating the Benefit

The household’s basic benefit is calculated by matching the income level (A-75%, B-100%, C-125%, D-150%, E-175%, and F-200% or 60% SMI) from the Income Guidelines (Attachment B) to the appropriate heating cost level as listed in the following Annual Heating Cost chart:

ANNUAL HEATING COST USAGE CATEGORY $3,500 or more AA $1,750 - $3,499 BB $1,000 - $1,749 CC Up to $1,000 DD

The income level and annual energy costs are then combined through the use of a Benefit Matrix. Below is an example; see Attachment D for the current year Benefit Matrix.

EXAMPLE MATRIX (DELIVERABLE FUELS) INCOME LEVEL USAGE CATEGORY A (75%) B (100%) C (125%) D (150%) E (175%) F (60% SMI) AA ($3,500+) 2,177 1,887 1,597 1,306 1,016 726 BB ($1,750-$3,499) 1,355 1,174 1,064 871 678 484 CC ($1,000-$1,749) 1,016 880 798 653 508 363 DD ($1-$1,000) 677 587 497 436 338 256

EXAMPLE MATRIX (UTILITIES)

INCOME LEVEL USAGE CATEGORY A (75%) B (100%) C (125%) D (150%) E (175%) F (60% SMI) AA ($3,500+) 1,361 1,180 999 817 635 454 BB ($1,750-$3,499) 847 734 665 545 424 303 CC ($1,000-$1,749) 635 550 499 409 318 227 DD ($1-$1,000) 424 367 311 273 212 160

For example, a one-person household with an income of $500/monthly who would fall under income level A on the Income Guidelines (Attachment B); and who had actual or estimated annual deliverable fuel energy usage of $1,800 that would fall under level BB on the Annual Heating Cost chart, would receive a benefit of $1,355 using the Benefit Matrix example above. The Benefit Matrix demonstrates how the highest level of assistance is provided to the lowest income households with the highest energy burden.

2026 - 2027 I PY27 NH Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) Procedures Manual 20 Completing the Application and Certifying as Eligible

When the program is open, all applications must be completed by intake staff within 30 days of the application date. If an applicant does not provide all of the required documentation within 30 days of the application date, the application will be denied for missing documentation. The applicant will be provided notification of what documents are still needed for completion and the application can be reopened if these missing documents are received.

An application can be certified eligible when all the questions on the application that are necessary for determination of eligibility are answered, and complete required documentation is attached.

Certifying an Application with a Benefit

Each application must then be reviewed and either denied or certified with a benefit within 30 days from of the date the intake staff member completed the application. Please note that applications experiencing an energy emergency require more immediate attention (see Energy Emergency Guidance).

A certifier reviews all applications for accuracy and completeness and determines eligibility or ineligibility based upon the information provided. The Certifier will indicate that a household is either eligible or ineligible by certifying the application with a benefit or denying the application. Upon certification, the Certifier must attest in ECOS that they have reviewed the application and it is complete. The certifier must be a different CAA staff person than the intake staff for that application.

Written notification of eligibility or denial must be sent to the applicant within 15 days of certification from opening of the program until April 30. When a household is found eligible for a FAP benefit, a Benefit Notification Letter (Attachment K) is sent to the applicant and to the vendor. When a household is ineligible for a FAP benefit, an Applicant Denial Letter (Attachment L) and a Fair Administrative Hearing Notice (Attachment M) are mailed to the applicant.

Copies of all correspondence pertaining to eligibility must be maintained and be easily accessible. ECOS will generate and save all system-generated letters, but any other correspondence pertaining to eligibility generated outside of ECOS must be maintained in ECOS files or notes. CAAs are not required to keep hard copies, but all program information including correspondence, applications, and reports and letters must be accessible for three years after the final expenditures for the applicable program year has ended.

2026 - 2027 I PY27 NH Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) Procedures Manual 21

6. ELIGIBILITY OF SPECIAL DWELLING OR INCOME CASES

The following procedures are to be used to determine eligibility for applicants with the following circumstances:

Campers/Mobile Home Dwellings

Residents in campers or mobile homes are ineligible to receive a Fuel Assistance benefit unless it is permanently attached to the ground. Acceptable documentation of permanent attachment includes: an invoice for mobile home park rent; a utility bill for service provided to the camper or mobile home; or a property tax bill.

Subsidized Housing

For FAP purposes, subsidized housing is defined as a rental unit with a rental amount that changes or is adjusted according to the tenant’s household income. Typically, the housing authority or housing program calculates the participant’s rent based on a percentage of income taking into consideration the type of dwelling, heating, cooling, and utility costs.

Tenants residing in subsidized housing will be eligible for benefits if they meet all other FAP requirements for eligibility, they are responsible for paying their own heating bill, and they have annual heating costs.

Subsidized Housing with Heat Included in Rent

Tenants residing in subsidized housing will not be eligible for benefits if their heat is included in the rent and they are not responsible for paying their own heating bill. The application should still be fully documented as these households may still be eligible for non-FAP funded Weatherization.

Fuel Tank in a Multi-unit Dwelling

When an applicant lives in a dwelling in which the fuel tank is shared amongst two or more separate units, please apply the benefit as below:

- If heat is included in rent, process with a landlord verification form and payment to landlord. - If heat is not included in rent and the applicant has a metered account for their unit, payment goes to the vendor.

2026 - 2027 I PY27 NH Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) Procedures Manual 22 - If the heat is not included in rent and there is no individual client account, make direct payment to the applicant. Income from Contracted and/or Seasonal Employees (i.e. Education)

Seasonal employees are hired annually for recurring periods of work that is less than twelve months a year due to their specific industry. Educational employees are the most common example; teachers and education staff may have a twelve-month contract but only work nine months of the year due to the nature of their work. While such income may be best reported for a twelve-month period, this type of employment has unique considerations.

Contracted salaried employees are paid through fixed compensation rather than an hourly wage. A salaried employee is paid the same amount regardless of exact hours worked and generally is not eligible for overtime pay. The contract may be for a twelve-month period, but the work may happen over fewer months. • Contractual, salaried employees should provide their current contract as income documentation. This may be a contract that begins after the application date (for example, if the applicant applies on August 1 but their contract begins on August 15). If a contract recently ended and they have not received a new contract, the most recent contract can be used provided it ended less than three months prior to application date. Contracts are commonly for twelve-month periods, but some, such as part-time faculty contracts at colleges, may be for a shorter duration.

Hourly seasonal employees may have a contract or no contract. School employees such as paraprofessionals, for example, may have a contract but be paid hourly for ‘up to’ a certain number of hours. An hourly contract may list the rate of pay and approximate hours, but hours and wages can fluctuate. • Hourly seasonal employees can provide documentation of current income through paystubs. If the employee is not currently working but intends to return to their seasonal position within the next three months (school employees in summer months, for example), other income documentation can be considered. Examples include documentation from employer, an upcoming contract, or the most recent W-2 (if the staff member was in the position the full prior year). If the employee was in a seasonal position previously but no longer intends to return to that position, prior income does not need to be considered.

Respite care programs provide reimbursement for service paid by the family member or caregiver to allow them time away from their challenging responsibility of taking care of the disabled or ill individual living in their household.

Given that respite care funds are provided on a reimbursement basis, it is not considered as income for the purposes of determining income eligibility.

Difficulty of care payments: This type of payment is defined as ‘payment to a family or household members of qualified disabled or chronically ill individuals who would be otherwise institutionalized. Payments are generally provided because the disability is so severe that the caretaker is unable to hold a job.’ Given the circumstances in which someone would receive such a payment, it is not considered as income for the purposes of determining income eligibility. This includes payment for room and board, which is not considered income.

Personal care services payments: This type of payment is defined as ‘payment to a family or household members of qualified disabled or chronically ill individuals for the day to day needs (bathing, dressing, eating etc) of the individual.’ Given the circumstances in which someone would receive such a payment, it is not considered as income for the purposes of determining income eligibility.

Child Support Paid

Child Support paid is considered an income expense if the person paying child support has documentation. Documentation examples include payroll deductions, verification from Child Support Hotline, copies of check stubs, etc. Documentation is required as this has an impact on eligibility and benefit amount.

If there is no documentation of the child support paid, it cannot be entered as an expense to reduce total income.

Child Support Received

Child Support received is not considered income. No documentation is needed if the household has other income sources that can cover their basic needs. However, if a household has no or very low income, the documentation of child support received (either on the application or through another method) is important. If a household member needs to complete a No or Low Income Declaration, staff can request verification of child support received as deemed necessary to help verify how the household is meeting their basic needs.

2026 - 2027 I PY27 NH Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) Procedures Manual 25 Self Employment

Income must be documented on an annual basis for all self-employed individuals. If an individual has not been self-employed for a full year, the total number of months from the start of the self-employment will be used to calculate income. Self-employed individuals must provide their most current federal tax return (Form 1040) along with all appropriate supporting schedules/forms to document their income from January 1 through December 31. After April 15 each year, the prior year tax return should be provided unless there is a documented copy of the tax filing extension.

• For sole proprietorships, Schedule C-EZ or Schedule C is required, with all attendant supporting forms such as Form 8829-Expenses for Business Use of Your Home and Form 4562-Depreciation and Amortization.

• For partnerships, Form 1065 is required, with all attendant Schedule K-1 forms and any other supporting forms such as Form 4562-Depreciation and Amortization and any statements for aggregated other deductions.

• For corporations, Form 1120 or 1120S is required, with all attendant supporting forms and schedules such as Form 1125A-Cost of Goods Sold, Schedule K-1 showing shareholders’ percentage of ownership in the corporation, Form 4562-Depreciation and Amortization, Form 8825-Rental Real Estate Income and Expenses of a Partnership or an S Corporation, and any statements for aggregated other deductions.

• For farm/agricultural businesses, Schedule F is required, with all attendant forms and schedules such as Form 4562- Depreciation and Amortization. Additional supporting documents may be requested upon review of the above documents to clarify the information represented.

There are some expenses that are not allowable for FAP. These may be included on the tax return but should not be entered as an expense into ECOS. Because of this, the total net profit or loss in ECOS may not match the total net profit or loss on the tax form. This includes:

• Depreciation (listed on Schedule C, Part II, item 13 OR on Form 4562) • Amortization (on Form 4562) • Business Use of Home (on Schedule C, this is in Part II, item 30) If the business address matches the home address on the application, this may indicate that some of the dwelling is used for business purposes. Staff should verify how many rooms, if any, are utilized for business purposes. This number of rooms should be subtracted from the FAP application.

2026 - 2027 I PY27 NH Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) Procedures Manual 27 Instructions for Completing the Self Employment Declaration

The following is a list of specific descriptions for the allowable deductions for self-employment income:

Advertising: Costs relating to business advertising in newspapers, radio, television, leaflets, brochures, etc. are deductible, with the exception of political ads and foreign advertising.

Bank Charges: The costs of maintaining a business bank account such as monthly service charges, check cashing charges, bad check charges, etc. are deductible.

Car & Truck: There are two methods for determining deductions: actual costs and standard mileage rate. If using the actual costs method, deduct gas, oil, tolls, tires, licenses, garage rent, parking fees, lease fees, and rental fees. If a car is used for both business and personal use, multiply the actual costs by the percent of time the car or truck is used for business. For example, a car used 60% of the time for business with $2,000 annual costs would have a $1,200 deduction (60% x $2,000 = $1,200). If using the standard mileage rate, multiply the business- related miles by the current IRS rate for mileage to arrive at the allowable deduction. Parking fees, tolls, and state and local personal property taxes may also be deducted. Records must be kept showing daily business mileage and a yearly business mileage figure.

Cleaning: The cost of cleaning and janitorial services is deductible.

Fuel: Fuel costs relating to the purchase of gasoline, diesel, gasohol, etc. used for work-related equipment are deductible (refer to the Car & Truck section below for transportation fuel).

Insurance: Payments for work-related insurance premiums are deductible, including premiums for fire, theft, flood, casualty, merchandise, inventory, liability, public liability, malpractice, worker's compensation, state unemployment insurance, use and occupancy, and business interruption. Employees' group insurance is also deductible as long as the strict nondiscrimination rules are complied with.

Interest: Interest payments on business loans, business credit cards (used to purchase strictly business items), and mortgages are deductible.

Office Expenses: The cost of office supplies for business are deductible as long as they are using within one year. Cost of rent and utilities associate with business office may also be deductible.

Postage: The cost of postage and shipping for business purposes are deductible.

2026 - 2027 I PY27 NH Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) Procedures Manual 28 Rent: Costs relating to the use of property that the applicant does not own such as cars, tools, equipment, and property are deductible.

Repairs: Minor costs relating to the repair of work-related property or equipment are deductible.

Supplies: The costs of incidental supplies and materials such as office supplies, tools, books, and professional equipment are deductible if they are normally used up within a year.

Taxes: Taxes relating to the cost of running a business or a profession are deductible, including sales, business profits, licenses, regulatory fees, state unemployment payments, corporate franchise taxes, user fees, and property taxes.

Travel: Normal expenses are deductible when traveling for business. Deductible expenses include airplane, bus, and train tickets, operating and maintaining vehicles (refer to the Car & Truck section), meals, lodging, and other ordinary and necessary expenses relating to business travel. Expenses that are lavish, extravagant, or for personal or vacation purposes cannot be deducted. Expenses for travel/commuting between home and office cannot be deducted.

Utilities: Normal costs associated with running an office or business are deductible, such as electricity, heating fuels, and telephone. Note: If a home office is used, only a cell phone used exclusively for business, a second phone line or actual long distance business phone calls are deductible.

Wages: Wages, salaries, bonuses, and gifts paid to employees, including anyone who is not a member of the household applying for the FAP, are deductible. In the case of household members on a payroll, be sure that their income is not counted twice.

Other: Bad business debts are deductible if there has been an actual loss of money or the amount of money to be paid was reported as income. Membership dues and subscriptions to professional, technical, or trade journals that deal with the applicant’s business are deductible. Legal and professional fees (i.e., accountants, lawyers, etc.) that are ordinary and necessary expenses of operating a business are deductible. Legal fees paid to acquire a business are not deductible. Penalties and fines resulting from the non-performance of a contract are deductible. However, fines and penalties resulting from criminal or legal action paid to any government agency are not deductible. The costs of medical insurance premiums are deductible at a 25 percent rate (i.e., $1,000 premium x 25% = $250 deduction). All deductions under the “Other” heading must be documented and have a schedule attached.

2026 - 2027 I PY27 NH Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) Procedures Manual 30 7. SHARED HOUSING AND HOUSEHOLD MEMBERS

Shared housing is a situation where two or more individuals reside in the same residence, but as separate households. These households may include individuals who are roomer/boarders, custodial caregivers, owners of rooming houses/divided residences, or persons receiving foster care payments for qualified individuals. The following descriptions provide guidance to the CAAs for evaluating the eligibility for an applicant in shared housing. All applications will first be based on the premise that a household consists of all individuals living within a residential unit. All other living situations will be evaluated on a case-by-case basis.

Roommates

A roommate is defined for FAP purposes as an individual who shares a residential unit with another individual(s), equally sharing energy expenses and living together as one economic unit. A roommate differs from a roomer/boarder because roommates share in the cost of the rent and share rented living quarters, while a roomer/boarder does not share living quarters. Roommates may have their names on the lease or may be unofficially subletting.

All roommates within a residential unit will be considered to be household members. The income for all roommates within a household will be calculated to determine FAP eligibility and the amount of the benefit.

In a situation where one residential unit is occupied by two separate individuals residing in fully separate living quarters with each individual being responsible for their own documented heating expenses, a waiver will be granted to regard them as non-roommates and separate households. Proof must be provided to document the two separate heating systems within the one unit, showing the separate account numbers in the names of the individually responsible parties for the unit’s heating expenses.

2026 - 2027 I PY27 NH Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) Procedures Manual 31 Roomers/Boarders (applicant rents room(s) from owner)

A roomer/boarder is defined for FAP purposes as an unrelated individual who lives in a specified room(s) within a boarding/rooming house or divided residence and who pays a stipulated amount for lodging, which may include kitchen privileges. The roomer/boarder must have at least one room for their own private use. A roomer/boarder must live independently without supportive services provided by the landlord or by any other member of the rooming house or divided residence. Roomers/boarders who pay for their lodging in either a commercial establishment or a private home that is their primary home may be eligible for LIHEAP benefits, including individuals staying in a hotel or motel long-term (for a minimum of one month prior to application date).

Roomers/Boarders cannot be related by blood, marriage or adoption to any member in the residence.

A roomer/boarder must provide a lease or other written agreement with the owner of the house and documentation of previously paid rent. A roomer/boarder must pay rent directly to the owner of the rooming house/divided residence. Only the number of rooms used by the roomer/boarder for private use should be included. Anyone whose name appears on a household energy account cannot be considered a roomer/boarder.

Rooming House/Divided Residence (applicant is owner who rents room or rooms)

When the owner of a rooming house/divided residence applies for fuel assistance, the following criteria will be used for determining eligibility: • In owner-occupied licensed homes, the owner will be considered self-employed. • Owner-occupied non-licensed homes will be treated as one household and income from all residents will be submitted and documented unless a resident(s) meet(s) the definition as a roomer/boarder.

A non-licensed home might be a private residence that has been divided (renting out a basement or in-law apartment, for example, or a bedroom). In a situation where the owner of the home is the applicant, the rental income must be included as income and any rooms used exclusively by the renter(s) should be excluded from total rooms on the owner’s application.

Note: Residents of institutions or community-based facilities that provide ongoing services, care, or treatment are not eligible to receive FAP benefits under either of the following circumstances: • A federal, state or local operating grant/subsidy is received by the institution or facility. • Residents do not otherwise personally experience an energy vulnerability which can be reduced by the FAP.

2026 - 2027 I PY27 NH Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) Procedures Manual 32 Child Residency When Custody is Shared

Children living with parents who share custody and maintain separate households can be counted as a household member in only one household each year. The parent who applies for assistance first may include the child in their household if they have primary or shared custody. If there is a dispute about which household should ‘claim’ the child on the application, applicants should provide court documentation such as physical custody orders or parenting plans to determine where the child resides the majority of the time. Parents can also take turns each year including the child in their household application.

If there is no parental rights/custody document in place or if shared custody is divided evenly (50/50), the applicant can provide documentation that may include, but is not limited to, verification from the school where the child is enrolled, DHHS award letter for SNAP or Cash Assistance that includes the child, a physician’s statement verifying residence on record, or day care provider statements verifying residence on record. Parents can also sign a Child Residency Agreement.

If custody is shared equally and the dispute cannot be resolved, the parent who applies earliest each year can include the children in the household.

2026 - 2027 I PY27 NH Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) Procedures Manual 33 Custodial Care Providers – Adult Care

A custodial care provider is defined for FAP purposes as a caregiver who lives with an elderly (60 and over) or disabled individual(s) solely for the purpose of providing essential health or supportive services to the elderly or disabled individual(s).

The custodial care provider will not be included as a household member on the application and the provider income will not be included in the total household income if either of the following conditions exists: • The custodial care provider has a primary residence somewhere else. • The custodial care provider gave up a primary residence for the sole purpose of giving care to the elderly or disabled individual(s).

The applicant must have a letter from a physician stating the medical need for an in-home provider. This procedure should only be utilized in cases when it is readily apparent to the CAA FAP Director that the elderly or disabled head of household's ability to remain in the home is dependent upon this relationship with the custodial care provider.

If an adult in custodial care resides within the care provider household (reverse live-in care, sometimes referred to as ‘Adult Foster Care’), the applicant household should provide documentation that shows they are the legal care provider (i.e. court documentation or home provider agreement). The person receiving care can either be excluded from the household or included in the household, whichever is more beneficial for the applicant household. If an adult receiving care is excluded from the household, the room(s) used exclusively by the adult in custodial care will not be included in calculating the number of rooms in the residence. If the adult receiving custodial care is included in the household, the income related to their care must also be included and all rooms in the household can be included.

In both situations described above, the care provider could be related or unrelated to the person they provide care for.

If a person is living in a long-term care facility/nursing home permanently, they would not be included in the household. Their income would be counted if it is received by the household member applying. If the person is in a nursing facility for temporary skilled rehabilitation (after a hospital stay, etc.), the person and their income would be counted.

Foster Care for Minors

Payments received by a home provider for foster care of a minor, made by either a state or tax- exempt placement agency, are reimbursements for the care of the foster individual and are not counted as income in determining income eligibility.

This regulation (IRS code) is specific to households with up to five individuals over age sixteen or up to ten individuals under age sixteen. The foster care individuals must reside in the provider’s home. The foster care individual is not included as a household member and the rooms used exclusively by the foster care individual(s) will not be included when calculating the number of rooms in a residential unit.

The total number of foster care individuals and the documentation of any foster care payments must be submitted with the application. If the payments do not document the names of individuals, documentation of foster care placement must be provided (e.g., copy of the state foster care certification).

Students

Students should only be included as a household member if they reside in the home full-time. If a student lives away from the household during the academic year they should not be counted as a household member. Any college or university student who is residing in the household should be included as a household member and their income should be counted. A student can only be listed as a household member on one application during any one FAP program year.

Foreign Students

Foreign students who are in the United States on a non-immigrant student VISA (Immigration and Naturalization Services, certificate I-20A-Visa Type/Class F1 or J1) and any of their dependents (Class F2 or J2) are not eligible for the FAP.

2026 - 2027 I PY27 NH Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) Procedures Manual 35 Qualified Noncitizens

As per federal law, US citizenship or lawfully admitted non-citizen status is a requirement to receive FAP. All lawfully admitted non-citizens, regardless of when they entered the United States, are eligible to receive FAP benefits if they meet all other eligibility requirements.

A qualified lawfully admitted noncitizen is any one of the following:

(i) A non-citizen lawfully admitted for permanent residence as an immigrant under the Immigration and Nationality Act (the “Act”) as defined in PRWORA.

(ii) An asylee granted asylum under section 208 of the Act.

(iii) A refugee admitted to the United States under section 207 of the Act.

(iv) A non-citizen paroled into the United States under section 212(d)(5) of the Act for a period of at least one year.

(v) A non-citizen whose deportation is being withheld under section 243(h) of the Act as in effect prior to April 1, 1997, or whose removal is being withheld under section 241(b)(3) of the Act.

(vi) A non-citizen granted conditional entry under section 203(a)(7) of the Act as in effect prior to April 1, 1980.

(vii) A non-citizen who is a Cuban or Haitian entrant; or

(viii) A non-citizen who (or whose child or parent) has been battered or subjected to extreme cruelty in the United States and otherwise satisfies the requirements of 8 U.S.C. §1641(c).

A noncitizen who is eligible due to their status as a lawful permanent resident (LPR), refugee, asylee, or other immigration status must provide documentation to show eligibility. Below are some examples of documentation that would indicate eligibility as a qualified noncitizen:

2026 - 2027 I PY27 NH Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) Procedures Manual 37 8. ENERGY EMERGENCY GUIDANCE

The New Hampshire Fuel Assistance Program procedures are intended to ensure that low- income households have access to services in a timely manner and access to emergency services on an immediate basis to prevent any household from experiencing a life-threatening hardship due to an energy emergency. The FAP definition of a response to an "energy emergency" is drawn directly from the federal Low Income Home Energy Assistance Act, as amended, 42 U.S.C. 2604.

The program shall be administered by public or nonprofit entities that have experience in administering energy crisis programs under the Low-Income Energy Assistance Act of 1980 or experience in assisting low-income individuals in the area to be served, the capacity to undertake a timely and effective energy crisis intervention program, and the ability to carry out the program in local communities. Upon receipt of the federal grant award and opening of the program, typically around December 1, the program shall:

• Prevent the loss of home energy when the applicant is at imminent risk of losing heat due to low fuel amounts, an impending disconnection, or an eviction notice if heat is included in rent. No later than 48 hours after a household applies for energy crisis benefits, the CAA will provide some form of assistance that will resolve the energy crisis if such household is eligible to receive such benefits and is facing an energy emergency but not a life-threatening situation.

• Restore home energy if the applicant has no heat. No later than 18 hours after a household applies for energy crisis benefits, provide some form of assistance that will restore the use of home energy if such household is eligible to receive such benefits and is in a life-threatening situation.

• Require each entity that administers such program to:

a) accept applications for energy crisis benefits at sites that are geographically accessible to all households in the area to be served by such entity; and

b) provide low-income individuals who are physically infirm with the means to submit applications for energy crisis benefits without leaving their residences or traveling to the sites at which such applications are accepted.

An energy emergency requiring a response within 48 hours after application may include applicants with low-heat, utility shut-off, or rental eviction.

2026 - 2027 I PY27 NH Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) Procedures Manual 38 A life-threatening energy emergency requiring a response within 18 hours after application will include applicants with no heat and may include applicants who are homeless.

At no time during the application process should a household go from an energy emergency to a life-threatening situation due to a delay in processing of an application.

All emergency applications must document the dates and times of the initial applicant contact, application, completion, certification, and authorization of emergency assistance.

If an applicant is experiencing an energy emergency, the following procedures will be followed: 1. An applicant in an energy emergency will have the opportunity to apply for fuel assistance within the next business day of the initial contact. The applicant in a life-threatening energy emergency will have the opportunity to apply for fuel assistance on the same business day as the initial contact.

2. The application for an energy emergency will be given priority. If eligible, notification will be made to the applicant's vendor immediately to authorize an emergency delivery or to guarantee payment in the case of a utility disconnection notice. Vendor confirmation of the notification must be documented.

3. If ineligible, the applicant will be notified and referred to an appropriate resource.

4. All eligible energy emergencies must be documented by dates and times of initial applicant contact, application, completion, certification, and authorization of emergency assistance.

2026 - 2027 I PY27 NH Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) Procedures Manual 39 9. ALTERNATIVE PROGRAMS

Assurance 16

The Federal Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) was reauthorized by Congress in the spring of 1994. In the reauthorization, Congress allowed new uses of "program" money up to 5% of the overall grant. The New Hampshire Fuel Assistance Program uses up to 5% of its available grant for Assurance 16 activities, which are specified by federal law to be:

• Counseling to promote self-sufficiency (case management - fiscal and energy related) • Needs assessments • Intervention on behalf of qualified households with energy suppliers

The primary goal of Assurance 16 is to work with a small percentage of FAP-eligible households to reduce or eliminate the need for the FAP or other assistance programs. The secondary goal is to target households with members who are elderly, disabled, or with children under the age of six that do not have sufficient means to provide for a healthy home environment and who may have artificially low home energy bills. The final goal is to help low-income people develop positive relationships with energy vendors.

The NH FAP Assurance 16 program provides self-sufficiency counseling to households that have required an expedited FAP application due to a home energy emergency (see section 8. Energy Emergency Guidelines). These households are encouraged to apply for the FAP and for other assistance in a timely manner to alleviate both special delivery charges and health and safety issues in the household.

Each CAA is required annually to submit an Assurance 16 proposal that demonstrates how the CAA plans to execute the provisions of Assurance 16. The proposal should be based on a year- round program, operating beyond the normal FAP year. The authority to use program money for this purpose is contingent upon the receipt of the Assurance 16 Plan proposal. The proposal must match the Assurance 16 activities that are being performed.

Each CAA will also provide a report on a regular basis, as specified by Federal and State requirements, which shows:

• How funds were spent • Number of households achieving self-sufficiency • Number of households reducing dependency on the FAP • Number of households denied benefits

2026 - 2027 I PY27 NH Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) Procedures Manual 40 The Senior Energy Assistance Services (SEAS)

The Senior Energy Assistance Services program funded by the New Hampshire Department of Health and Human Services, Bureau of Adult and Elderly Services provides energy assistance in the form of a $270.38 benefit to the primary heating source for deliverable fuels, electricity, natural gas, or wood for households with a member aged 60 or older and who is not eligible for the NH Fuel Assistance Program due to being over-income for the normal FAP benefit.

To qualify for a SEAS benefit, applicants must complete a FAP/WAP application and be found ineligible for FAP/WAP benefits by regular program guidelines. The CAAs must determine eligibility for SEAS through need or hardship, which is to be documented by the CAA.

CAAs must use the specific SEAS Reimbursement Request for these funds and provide accompanying documentation to NH DOE with household and expenditure information.

Supplemental Benefit Program

When funds are available, New Hampshire’s Fuel Assistance Program may include a Supplemental Benefit to provide additional assistance to previously certified eligible households. This benefit would be based upon several factors including, but not limited to, the availability of funds, the number of applicant households, the increased cost of home energy, and the development of operating procedures specific to this programmatic component.

2026 - 2027 I PY27 NH Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) Procedures Manual 41 10. APPLICANT RIGHTS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Confidentiality

It is of the utmost importance that applicants are guaranteed complete confidentiality regarding information disclosed to all persons involved in the administration of the FAP.

The applicant agrees to a release of information when completing and signing the FAP application form. This release is specific to FAP and includes the following only:

• Information necessary to establish eligibility for the FAP • Information necessary to determine the amount and type of assistance • Information necessary to perform program evaluation and analysis • Sharing of information with the NH Electric Assistance Program and Weatherization Assistance Program for purposes of eligibility for that program

All other sharing of information requires an additional specific release signed by the applicant or other household member or a legal subpoena.

Personally Identifiable Information

Information that can be used to identify a particular person or household is known as PII – Personally Identifiable Information. This includes a person’s name, SSN, date of birth, and address. An important component of ensuring confidentiality is adopting best practices for keeping PII safe. CAAs should have measures in place to protect the accidental transfer of this information. This includes policies for physical and electronic information. Some examples:

• Only print information with PII when necessary • Physical files containing PII should be secured • Limit the use of PII in email by referencing application numbers or initials • Encrypt any emails that must contain PII • Prevent access by creating strong passwords and locking computer screens when away Complaints

If an applicant believes there has been a violation regarding their data and wishes to share concern with how their information has been disclosed, they should contact the FAP director at the CAA where they applied. There is no penalty for filing a complaint. Should the applicant feel their concern is unresolved at the CAA, they can contact the NH Department of Energy at 603- 271-3670 or via email at fuelassistance@energy.nh.gov.

2026 - 2027 I PY27 NH Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) Procedures Manual 42 Appeal and Fair Administrative Hearing Procedures

All Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) applicants who have been denied, who question the FAP benefits provided, and/or question the timely processing of their application are entitled to appeal the decision, which may include a Fair Administrative Hearing. All applicants/ will be provided with information regarding the appeal process and the FAP Fair Administrative Hearing Procedures (Attachment M). The CAA must provide written notification of either the denial of benefits or the benefit determination to all FAP applicants.

The written notification to FAP applicants who are denied benefits must include the following: • A brief statement of the reason(s) for denial of benefits • A brief explanation of the applicant’s right to appeal process • A brief explanation of the appeal and Fair Administrative Hearing process

An applicant is entitled to appeal the FAP benefit determination for any of the following reasons: • Application has been denied • Application was neither denied nor approved within 60 days of the application date during the period of time the program is open (typically Dec 1 – April 30) • Benefit amount is less than what the applicant believes should have been awarded • The benefit amount or the duration of the benefit is less than what the written CAA notification originally identified

A FAP applicant may appeal the determination of benefits by contacting the CAA FAP Director and requesting a review of the application within 30 days of receiving the determination letter. The CAA FAP Director must meet with the applicant in-person or via a virtual/phone meeting within 10 days of the applicant’s request for an appeal.

During the meeting between the applicant and the CAA FAP Director, the applicant will have an opportunity to express any concerns and the CAA FAP Director will have an opportunity to review and attempt to resolve the dispute. The CAA is responsible for documenting the results of the meeting. The documentation must contain information relative to the eligibility requirements or benefit determination.

If the applicant is not satisfied with the outcome of the meeting, the CAA FAP Director must next refer the applicant to the NH DOE FAP Administrator for an additional review. The CAA FAP Director must communicate the history of the appeal, including the documentation of their meeting with the applicant. The NH DOE FAP Administrator must meet with the applicant in- person or via a virtual/phone meeting within 10 days of the applicant request for a second review of the application.

2026 - 2027 I PY27 NH Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) Procedures Manual 43 If the applicant is not satisfied with the determination of FAP benefits after discussing the issue with the CAA FAP Director and the NH DOE FAP Administrator, the applicant may request a Fair Administrative Hearing. An applicant must request a Fair Administrative Hearing with NH DOE within 30 business days of the exchange with the NH DOE FAP Administrator.

The NH DOE Fair Administrative Hearings will meet the following standards:

• All hearings shall be held in a location reasonably convenient to the applicant. • The hearing officer shall be a NH DOE employee who was not involved in rendering the challenged action or decision. • The NH DOE hearing officer shall review the applicant CAA file prior to the hearing. The hearing officer shall review the applicant file prior to the hearing, including: a) FAP application, including supporting household and income documentation b) Written notification to the applicant of denial or any other contested decision c) Notes and/or documentation containing information relied upon by FAP staff in making the decision to deny benefits or to take the contested action • The hearing will be recorded by NH DOE and the decision will be based upon the record and any relevant evidence and information introduced during the hearing.

The applicant is entitled to:

• Review CAA documents prior to the hearing. NH DOE will ensure that the applicant is provided with this option in a timely manner. • A copy of the current FAP Policy and Procedures Manual. The manual is available online at the NH DOE website, but the NH DOE will provide a printed copy of the manual if it is requested by the applicant. • Request an interpreter to be provided and funded by NH DOE. • Bring a representative to accompany him/her to the hearing; however, NH DOE is not required to provide or to pay for such a representative. • Present oral testimony, a written statement, and/or other relevant evidence. • Present witnesses and cross-examine witnesses.

The NH DOE will adhere to the following requirements:

• The applicant has 30 days from the applicant’s meeting with the NH DOE FAP Administrator to request a hearing in writing. • The NH DOE will conduct a hearing within 20 business days of receipt of the written request.

2026 - 2027 I PY27 NH Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) Procedures Manual 45 11. FRAUD PREVENTION AND RESPONSE

Fraud Prevention and Reporting

Fraud is an event of suspected intentional deception, omission, or concealment made for business or personal gain, to assist or harm others and/or to misuse program funds. CAAs must have internal controls to take reasonable steps to prevent fraud by applicants, employees, and energy vendors. This includes but is not limited to:

• Separation of duties for application intake, data entry, verification and certification, and benefit payments • Self-monitoring activities to reduce, find, and correct errors that may occur during intake, certification, and fiscal activities • Ensuring policies are in place regarding how fraudulent claims will be handled • Taking action when credible reports of fraud are received If any CAA employee or FAP applicant suspects fraud they should make a report to either the FAP Director at the CAA or directly to the NH Department of Energy. This may be a concern about misinformation from applicants or any concerns about fraud by any CAA staff. It could also include any concerns about fraud or abuse by their energy vendor in regards to their FAP benefit, such as not crediting the entire benefit to the account.

Fuel Assistance vendors sign an agreement in order to participate in the program. They agree to keep customers’ participation in the program confidential, to not treat customers adversely because of the assistance and to not discriminate in the cost or related services for any customers receiving FAP assistance. They also agree to apply any FAP benefit appropriately and to maintain accurate records. If anyone is concerned that a vendor is not meeting these requirements, they should make a report to either the FAP Director at the CAA or directly to the NH Department of Energy.

Conflict of Interest

Any application for a current CAA employee, relative of a CAA employee, former CAA employee, or a friend of that CAA employee shall be reviewed and approved by a staff person at a supervisory level or higher. Staff members should not be involved in the processing of an application for family members or friends with whom they have an established relationship.

By signing this application, I acknowledge that I have read and understand all the terms and conditions outlined in the program requirements and agree to comply with all rules and regulations set forth by the program administrators. I confirm that all members of the household are listed along with all sources of income. I authorize the Fuel, Electric, and Weatherization Assistance Programs to contact any necessary third party to collect and verify household income and energy usage. I authorize the verification of all information provided and consent to the collection, storage, and processing of my personal data for the purpose of program evaluation and reporting.

I hereby attest under penalty of perjury that all information provided in this application for the program is true, accurate, and complete to the best of my knowledge. I understand that if I knowingly give inaccurate or incomplete information pertaining to my eligibility for the program(s), I am breaking the law and can be prosecuted; conviction may result in imprisonment and/or fine. Furthermore, I may be subject to administrative penalties which may include denial of eligibility and/or repayment of the assistance I received.

Misrepresentation may occur during the application process because of misunderstandings or ignorance. Third party information to the CAA may also conflict with what the applicant has stated on the application.

A notification of potential fraud might come from a CAA employee, the NH DOE, or a member of the public. Regardless of the source, the FAP Director/Manager should immediately act when informed of potential fraud on an application, including any conflicts with:

• Third party information • Documentation provided • Verbal information provided by the applicant

Since a discrepancy may be the result of unintentional misinformation or misunderstandings, CAAs should follow the review processes outlined below when a discrepancy in the application has been identified. The CAA will hold funds in the amount of the benefit in question in reserve pending the outcome of the review process.

2026 - 2027 I PY27 NH Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) Procedures Manual 54 Authorization to Spend

FAP funds are contracted to the CAAs but are available only as the federal funds are awarded to the State. The State gives authorization to the CAA to spend funds by the issuance of the Authorization to Spend (Attachment I) only after contracts are approved by Governor and Executive Council and the federal funding has been received by the state of New Hampshire.

Over-awarding (aka Over-obligating)

In the course of the program year, a CAA may reach the maximum level of the original Authorization to Spend, and it may become necessary to make a request to NH DOE for approval to provide additional program funds.

The CAA must receive prior authorization to spend additional funds from the NH DOE FAP Administrator and must follow the following procedures:

1. The CAA FAP Director will contact the NH DOE FAP Administrator to discuss current program status which will include past program history, current applications in process, appointments in advance as well as projected program activity.

2. THE NH DOE will provide a written decision on the approval or denial which will be sent to the CAA FAP Director.

A CAA that over-spends program funds without prior written approval may be required to use administrative funds to cover the amount of unapproved funds.

Reallocation

NH DOE may reallocate unobligated program funds when an imbalance in program fund availability occurs between CAAs. An imbalance in program funds occurs when CAA "A" has unspent funds above the amount needed to fund eligible household benefits, while CAA "B" has unspent funds below the amount needed to fund eligible household benefits. This reallocation will be executed by the NH DOE with advanced notice.

2026 - 2027 I PY27 NH Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) Procedures Manual 55 13. BENEFIT NOTIFICATION AND PAYMENT PROCEDURES

Benefit Notification

Enrolled applicants are notified by a Benefit Notification Letter that they were enrolled in the program. The letter will provide the benefit amount and the name of the vendor (or landlord) who will receive the payment. The Benefit Notification Letter also informs clients of the date that the awarded benefits will expire. After the expiration date, any remaining credit balances are rolled back into the program.

The energy supplier is notified of the benefit amount by receiving a Vendor Notification Letter (Attachment N) within 10 working days from the eligible household’s application certification date or the opening of the program on/around December 1. This letter will contain the applicant’s information, including account information, as well as the amount of the benefit.

Benefit Payments

The CAA will make payment of the full benefit amount within 30 calendar days of the date on the vendor notification letter. Services rendered prior to October 1 of each year by vendors of deliverable fuels are not an allowable payment except in the case of wood deliveries, which may be authorized for delivery after July 1.

If a vendor is refusing delivery due to a prior balance, CAAs may request a waiver for the payment to be applied for deliveries made prior to October 1. No payments may be made beyond the final payment date established at the end of each program year without an approved written waiver from NH DOE.

Transfer and Sale of Benefits

The FAP benefit may not be sold, released, or otherwise transferred by the recipient or the energy supplier. Only the CAA may authorize a transfer of the benefit from one vendor to another when the transfer is necessary to allow the applicant to use the benefit and the transfer is consistent with all FAP guidelines.

2026 - 2027 I PY27 NH Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) Procedures Manual 56 Change of Vendor or Address / Transfer of Benefit

Transfer of benefit amounts will be limited to any of the following situations:

• A household moves and their vendor does not serve their new area of new fuel type • A household moves and now has heat included with their rent • A household has a change in heating system and their chosen vendor does not serve this fuel type (e.g. a household receives weatherization assistance and a new heating system) • A household’s chosen vendor is refusing to serve the household • There is another significant circumstance that justifies the change o FAP manager/director or designee approval required

If a client moves to a new address but continues to utilize the same vendor for their energy needs, the benefit can remain on the applicant’s account.

If a household with heat included in rent moves before the full benefit is applied to rent, the landlord is expected to refund directly to the applicant any amount not already applied to rent owed.

If a vendor sends a refund to the Community Action agency, the agency can reissue the remaining amount of the benefit to the household if they continue to reside in New Hampshire and continue to have a documented home-heating responsibility. A household would submit a Change of Address/Vendor form along with documentation of their new heating vendor. The funds can then be reissued to the new vendor. Benefits can only be reissued to households residing in an eligible residence.

If a vendor refund is for a household who moved from a residence with a direct heating cost to a residence with heat included, the remaining benefit can be reissued either as a direct payment to the applicant or to their electric vendor if the account is in a household member’s name.

If there is a change in household composition, the benefit will stay with the original dwelling unit. If any member of the original household is in the original residence, the benefit stays with the dwelling. If all household members move, the benefit will follow the applicant.

If the household does not meet any of these criteria, the refund should be submitted to the NH DOE (see section on benefit returns).

2026 - 2027 I PY27 NH Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) Procedures Manual 57 Heat Included in Rent Payment

For applicants whose heat is included in the rent, a Landlord Verification form (Attachment J) must document the amount of the rent per month and must have a signature from the property owner/landlord that signifies they have reviewed the agreement on the form. As the agreement on the Landlord Verification form outlines, the property owner agrees to apply the full benefit amount to rent, reducing the rent by the amount of the payment. Should the tenant move out before the full amount of the benefit is utilized, the owner agrees to refund any unused portion of the benefit to the tenant directly.

At least every other year, a valid W-9 form should be requested from the landlord and kept on file before payments are made to confirm the payee’s name and address have not changed.

Direct Payments

Direct payments to the client may be made in extenuating circumstances. A waiver is required in these cases, with written approval from the NH DOE FAP Administrator or designee required before payment. EXCEPTION: No waiver is required if the direct payment is going to a FANF household whose cash assistance benefit is paid directly to the landlord.

Other Allowable Payments

Other allowable payments are those that are incidental to the start-up of service including reasonable connection or re-connection fees, delivery fees (including off-hour delivery charges), deposits, tank setting or priming fees, reconnection fees, tariff charges, and other fees related to the start-up of service. Certified eligible homeowner households can choose to have up to $300 of their benefit pay for furnace repair or cleaning costs by their chosen vendor. This would include payments of up to $300 toward a service plan that provides annual cleaning/tune-up and potential repairs. The FAP Benefit cannot be used for security deposits, finance charges, or tank leasing or rental.

Deceased Clients

No benefit should be issued or paid to an applicant who is deceased. If an agency learns that an applicant is deceased and they were the only member of their household, the application should be denied and no benefit should be paid. If the benefit has already been awarded and paid for a certified client who is now deceased, expenses incurred prior to and during the 30 days following the date of death can be paid.

Each program year, all deliverable fuel and utility vendors are sent a new Vendor Agreement. This Vendor Agreement includes stipulations regarding when FAP benefit funds must be refunded. These benefit refunds, also known as benefit returns, are then deposited into the CAA FAP account to be reissued or returned to the NH DOE.

Refunds from Vendors to CAA

If an account is closed with FAP benefit funds remaining, the participating vendor must return the funds to the CAA within 30 calendar days. It is not the intent that the customer should be reimbursed by the vendor. However, a customer closing an account may be reimbursed for a previously paid bill with approval from the CAA once it is verified that it is the customer funds, not FAP funds, that are being reimbursed.

For all benefits returned the vendor must identify the household name, case number and program year, and the reason the funds are being returned. The program year listed should be the program year when the benefits were awarded. For example, if a benefit was returned to a CAA in January 2026 (PY 2025-26) but was initially paid to a vendor in January 2025 (PY 2024- 25), the correct program year is PY 2024-25. This is important as benefits are governed by different rules during the active contract timeline versus after the CAA contract expiration.

2026 - 2027 I PY27 NH Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) Procedures Manual 60 15. EXPENDITURES AND PROCUREMENT

Fuel Assistance Program Expenditures

Each CAA will be asked to create a budget for the program year and the budget will consist of multiple types of expenditures:

• Program – These funds are limited to direct benefit payment for enrolled households. • Administrative – These funds are utilized for expenditures categorized as “Admin” expenses, including supplies, rent, mileage, postage, salaries and wages, and more. • Program Support – These funds are limited to salaries and wages only that are indirect program costs directly related to engagement and enrollment of clients. • Assurance 16 – These funds can be used for direct client services only - salaries, wages, and fringe benefits for staff who are completing Assurance 16 activities. CAA contracts will outline how much is available in each of these categories. FAP Directors at the CAAs will submit a proposed budget at the start of each program year utilizing budget templates for Administrative, Program Support, and Assurance 16 funding. The templates will be provided by NH DOE. Reimbursement requests for these three expenditures must be submitted monthly showing the actual cost of administering FAP at their agency.

Because the LIHEAP statute limits the state use for Administrative funds to not exceed 10% in a given program year, the budget templates must list any other Federal resources used by the agency to support FAP. CAAs must submit a request in writing to the DOE before using any other Federal funds (i.e. CSBG) in the administration of FAP. The state must ensure the total amount of Federal funds used to administer FAP must not exceed 10%.

Program Support Funds Program Support funding may be used for staff time spent on:

• Outreach • Prescreening and intake activities • System data entry and updating • File review • Intake appointments and interviews regardless of venue, including office, home visits, phone appointments, or other virtual visits • Associated fringe benefits and payroll taxes associated with the listed activities about In theory, these activities should closely align with the activities done by front line intake staff.
