2026 - 2027 I PY27 NH Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) Procedures Manual 63 16. MONITORING

NH DOE will conduct program and fiscal monitoring of the CAAs for compliance with Federal and State rules and regulations. NH DOE is available for training and technical assistance if further assistance is needed.

On-site and desk monitoring will occur throughout the program year. Each on-site visit will include an entrance and exit interview between the NH DOE monitor and CAA staff. The FAP Director/Manager or a designee should attend, though others are encouraged to join, including the agency CEO, CFO, or COO. If follow-up or corrective action is required, a time frame for corrective action will be given in this report.

Monitoring of energy suppliers may be done by an NH DOE monitor on a random basis for compliance with Federal and State rules and regulations. NH DOE will issue a written report to the CAAs containing all findings following each monitoring visit of a vendor in their territory.

In the case of failure to adhere to the rules and regulations, the CAA will request training and technical assistance and/or develop a corrective action plan and act upon said plan within an amount of time agreed upon by NH DOE. Upon review and consideration of the corrective action to bring about a resolution, NH DOE will notify the CAA of its acceptance or denial and offer further technical assistance.

Failure to correct any questionable matter will result in the following:

• Non-compliance will be brought to the attention of NH DOE. • All grant payments to a sub-grantee may be withheld until non-compliance is resolved. • The NH FAP Administrator or designee will bring the non-compliance to the immediate attention of the Executive Director of the CAA.

The CAA will retain FAP program funds in a specified account and funds cannot be comingled with other funding sources. By the 15th of each month, an updated monthly bank statement for the FAP account must be shared with NH DOE. This monthly bank statement must document any interest earned. The CAA is to spend earned interest on the Fuel Assistance Program.

Monitoring by NH DOE may include but is not limited to:

Intake Site Evaluation • Adequacy of sites – number of staff and hours covered • Accessibility of intake via sites and telephone • Information given to applicants, privacy for applicants • Politeness/sensitivity and referrals to other social services/organizations

Program Monitoring Reports

NH DOE will provide the subgrantee with a written report within 30 days of each on-site monitoring visit. The following definitions may assist the CAAs in fully addressing the issues in the monitoring report:

Issues of Non-Compliance An issue of non-compliance will be noted where practices are found to not meet the state requirements. An issue of non-compliance is one that is not in alignment with a policy or procedure that is outlined in our NH state manual. The section of the manual outlining the related policy or procedure will be documented along with the specific issues of non- compliance. Sample issues of non-compliance may include not meeting required timeframes for application certification or energy emergency responses or not documenting income according to the manual. Any issues of non-compliance will require immediate attention, including a Corrective Action Plan to be submitted to the NH DOE within 30 days. The NH DOE will respond to all Corrective Action Plan submissions indicating whether or not the NH DOE is satisfied that all issues of non-compliance have been addressed.

Opportunities for Improvement Opportunities for improvement will highlight areas where there may be an opportunity to enhance or expand a current process or policy to better administer the program. These are not areas out of compliance with the manual, but rather opportunities to improve the effectiveness of the staff or program management through use of best practices. Examples may include recommendations for process improvement, training, or other programmatic components. These are recommendations to consider for implementation that do not require a corrective action plan response.

2026 - 2027 I PY27 NH Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) Procedures Manual 66 17. REPORTING

As a federal program, there are many important documentation and reporting requirements for the Fuel Assistance Program. The CAAs are responsible for submitting all required reports to the NH DOE in a timely manner. Reports are expected to be submitted on time, complete and accurate. This section will outline requirements as well as provide descriptions and due dates for the most common requirements. This is not an exhaustive list and requests for documentation may be made from the NH DOE to the CAAs throughout the year.

• Weekly Reimbursement Request Report: CAAs are required to submit weekly reimbursement request reports to DOE each Monday by 10am. The report will be submitted via ECOS unless instructed otherwise. This weekly report provides financial information related to program funds awarded and refunds received in the prior week. Upon review, the DOE staff will either approve or reject the request. If rejected, a reason will be provided. Once approved, the CAA will have access to the information needed to provide benefit letters and payments for the households included in that week’s report.

• Outreach Plan and Quarterly Reports – Each CAA is responsible for creating a plan each new program year that documents the outreach they will provide to their communities. This plan includes information about their outreach center locations as well as planned activities and outreach campaigns. A quarterly report provides updates throughout the year on how the plan is being implemented.

• Assurance 16 Plan and Reports – Each CAA utilizing Assurance 16 funding is responsible for creating a plan for how they will implement Assurance 16 at their agency. The agency must identify the Assurance 16 households and provide updates on the outcomes with these designated households (Attachment O).

• Monthly Reimbursement Request Reports – Each CAA will provide monthly reports on the financial program management. Toward the start of each program year, each CAA will create a proposed budget for the year based on the amount provided in the new program year contract. This proposed budget will include amounts for Administrative, Assurance 16, and Program Support funds. Monthly reimbursement reports will be required for all three. Reimbursement reports will also be required at least once a quarter for any SEAS program reimbursements. Monthly reports are due by the 15th of the following month. The final month of the contract (September) additional time is allotted; CAAs have 30 days to submit this final close out month.

PY27 Fuel Assistance Program Benefit Determination In NH, the FAP benefit amount awarded to eligible households is based on two factors: Household Income + Annual Heating Cost

The Benefit Matrix is designed so that the highest level of assistance will be furnished to those households which have the lowest incomes and the highest energy costs.

Below is an example of the Benefit Matrix. Across the top you can see the six income tiers make up six columns. On the left, you can see four rows that match the heating cost tiers.

As an example: a household with annual heating costs of $1,700 would get a different benefit amount depending on the household income. • Less than 75% of the federal poverty amount? Column A - benefit of $1,460 • Between 150-175% of the federal poverty amount? Column E - benefit of $730

Fuel and Electric Assistance Program Self Employment Information

You are self-employed if you: • Work for yourself in any capacity. Some examples include running errands, selling goods online, delivery services, lawn care, renting property, or providing services and/or freelance work. • Carry on a trade or business as a sole proprietor or independent contractor • Earn rental income from a property (or properties) you own • Are a member of a partnership that carries on a trade or business You can be self-employed working full-time or part-time.

Applicants who are self-employed are required to provide all documentation for the prior 365 days of income. Generally, this can be provided with a complete copy of the current year tax return with all schedules included.

A few notes for self-employed applicants: • Self-employment should be documented through tax statements even if the net profit is negative or $0. If the losses are greater than the profit, the lowest income will be recorded is $0. • Depreciation deductions are not an allowable expense and will be added back into the net profit. • When a business is operated out of a person’s residence, be it owned or rented, staff will be required to use statewide policy to exclude these rooms from household for benefit.

Instructions on how to complete the deductions section of the Self-Employment Declaration

• Advertising: Costs related to advertising business in newspapers, radio, television, social media, brochures, etc, are deductible • Bank Charges: The cost of maintaining a business bank account is deductible (i.e. monthly service charges, check cashing charges, bad check charges, etc). • Car/Truck: There are two methods for determining deductions: Actual Costs and Standard Mileage Rate. o Actual Costs: Deduct the actual costs of gas, oil, tolls, tires, licenses, garage rent, parking fees, lease fees, and rental fees. If a car is used for both business and personal use, multiply the actual costs by the percent of time the car/truck is used for business. *A car that is used for 60% of the time for business with $2,000 annual costs would have a $1,200 deduction (60% X 2000 = 1200). o Standard Mileage: If using the standard mileage rate, multiply the business related miles by the current IRS rate for a mileage to arrive at the allowable deduction. You may also deduct parking fees, tolls, state and local personal property taxes. Records must be kept showing daily business mileage and a yearly business mileage figure. • Cleaning: The cost of cleaning and janitorial services for business are deductible. • Fuel: Fuel costs relating to gasoline/diesel used for work related equipment other than vehicle (e.g. tractor) • Insurance: The cost of work-related insurance premiums are deductible including premiums for fire, theft, flood, casualty, merchandise, inventory, liability, public liability, malpractice, worker’s compensation, state unemployment insurance, use and occupancy and business interruption. Employees’ group insurance is also deductible as long as the strict nondiscrimination rules are complied with. • Interest: Any interest paid on business loans, business credit cards, and mortgages for business. Must all be used exclusively for business purposes to be deductible. • Office Expenses: The cost of office supplies used for business are deductible as long as they are used within one year. Cost of rent and utilities associated with business office may also be deductible. • Postage: The cost of postage and shipping for business purposes are deductible. • Rent: The cost to use property for business purposes that you do not own (i.e. cars, tools, property, etc) • Supplies: The cost of incidental supplies and materials used for business (such as tools, office supplies, and equipment) are deductible if they are used within one year. • Taxes: Taxes related to the cost of running business/profession are deductible, including sales, business profits, licenses, regulatory fees, state unemployment payments, franchise, user fees, and property. • Travel: Normal expenses are deductible when traveling for business. Deductible expenses include: airplane, bus and train tickets, operating and maintaining vehicles (refer to CAR and TRUCK section), meals, lodging, and other ordinary and necessary expenses relating to business travel. Expenses that are lavish, extravagant, or are for personal/vacation purposes cannot be deducted. Expenses for travel/commuting between home and office cannot be deducted. • Utilities: Normal costs associated with running a business are deductible, such as electricity, heating, and telephone. Note: if a home office is used, only a second phone line specifically for business is deductible. • Wages: Any wages, salaries, or bonuses paid to employees who are NOT a member of the household are deductible. Wages paid to self or any household members are not deductible. • Other: Other items that may be deductible include membership dues, subscriptions to relevant technical or trade journals, legal and professional fees (lawyers or accountants – not including legal fees paid to acquire business), minor costs related to the repair of work related equipment, cost of medical insurance premiums are deductible at a 25% rate (i.e. $1,000 premium = $250 deductible expense). Bad business debts are deductible if there has been an actual loss of money.

Section 5.

PAYMENT PROCEDURES AND USE OF FUNDS The Supplier will identify all subsidiaries and branch offices providing Home Energy under this Agreement by completing Attachment 1, Listing of Supplier's Subsidiaries and Branch Offices.

The Supplier will receive notification of FAP Benefits and will be sent payment of Benefit amount for each Eligible Household as a one-time payment to be applied as a credit to the Supplier’s account for that Eligible Household. The Benefit amount should be utilized until expended or expired.

This credit can be applied to any deliveries or services on or after the start of the program year (October 1, 2026) for Suppliers with deliverable Home Energy. The FAP Benefit can pay for the cost of Home Energy products as well as fees related to the start-up of service, delivery, tank setting or priming fees, reconnection fees, and tariff charges. The FAP Benefit cannot be used for security deposits, finance charges, or tank leasing or rental. There will be an annual request for a list of Eligible Households along with any remaining Benefit balance.

The Subgrantee is required to pay the Supplier within 30 calendar days after notification of the Benefit is sent. The Supplier will return any duplicate payments received on behalf of any Eligible Household to Subgrantee in the same FAP program year.

Section 6.

RECORDS

The Supplier will maintain an accounting system for fiscal records covering all Home Energy supplied and Benefits received and applied to the accounts of Eligible Households under this Vendor Agreement for a period of three years from the effective credit dates. The Supplier’s records will indicate:

1. The amount of Home Energy delivered to Eligible Households; and 2. The amount of the Benefit payments for Home Energy made on behalf of the Eligible Household by the Subgrantee.

The Supplier, upon written request from the FAP administrator, Subgrantee, or an Eligible Household (with regard to their own account) will promptly provide a status report indicating:

1. The Benefit amount of an Eligible Household received by Supplier; 2. The Home Energy supplied to date to an Eligible Household; and 3. The amount of Benefit received by Supplier and remaining in an account for the Eligible Household.

A FAP or Subgrantee representative may, during the Supplier’s normal business hours, inspect and copy, at its own expense, the Supplier’s records that pertain only to Eligible Households receiving FAP Benefits.

NON-DISCRIMINATION & ADVERTISING

The Supplier shall not advertise in a manner that implies that FAP assistance is available only through that Supplier, or that FAP applications are taken by the Supplier, or that in any other way misleads the public about the FAP.

The Supplier also agrees to respect the confidentiality of Eligible Households.

Section 8.

FUEL ASSISTANCE CONTRACT DURATION & TERMINATION

The Supplier agrees to notify the Subgrantee and the NH Fuel Assistance Program if it is not able to fulfill any or all of the requirements in this Vendor Agreement at any time.

The Supplier’s failure to comply with any of the provisions of this Vendor Agreement shall, at the sole option of the FAP, enable the FAP to terminate this Vendor Agreement without liability thereto, and shall entitle the FAP to bar the Supplier from participation in future Fuel Assistance Programs administered by the State of New Hampshire and to avail itself of any other remedies available under any applicable law. The Supplier must notify the Subgrantee at least 120 days before filing for bankruptcy or closure of the business and must return all Benefit funds provided to the Supplier by Subgrantee and not expended on Eligible Household accounts at least 91 days before filing for bankruptcy and/or closure.

This Vendor Agreement shall be in effect until midnight August 1, 2028 (when all PY27 benefits should be expended or returned). The Supplier, its successors and its assignees, agree that the rights of Eligible Households which have received Home Energy under this Vendor Agreement shall not be prejudiced in the event of early termination of said agreement. In the event of early termination of this Vendor Agreement, the Supplier shall return all FAP funds provided to the Supplier by Subgrantee and not expended on Eligible Household accounts within 30 days from termination to the Subgrantee.

Section 9.

GOVERNMENT REQUIREMENTS

The terms of this Vendor Agreement and its execution are subject to applicable laws and regulations of the State of New Hampshire. No eligible household will be treated adversely because of such assistance under applicable New Hampshire law.

Section 1. DEFINITIONS

(1) The term “Subgrantee” means the above-mentioned Community Action Agency, the Tri- County Community Action Program (TCCAP), in the State of New Hampshire.

(2) The term “Supplier” means the above-named company, which supplies Home Energy directly to an Eligible Household.

• The Supplier will charge the Eligible Household, in the normal billing process, any difference between the actual cost of the Home Energy and the amount of the Payment made by the Subgrantee of the State of New Hampshire Fuel Assistance Program.

• The FAP Program Year 2026-2027 (PY 27) wood delivery period begins on July 1, 2026. PY27 FAP Benefits can be used for any wood delivery made on or after this date. The Benefit is available for use during the Program Year of the receipt and the Program Year immediately following. PY27 Program Year funds expire after May 31, 2028. Any PY27 Benefit amount remaining unspent at this time must be refunded by the Supplier to the Subgrantee by August 1, 2028.

Section 3. PAYMENT PROCEDURES

The Subgrantee is required to pay the Supplier within 30 calendar days after notification of the Benefit is sent. The Payment sent will be the full Benefit amount to be applied to the customer’s account as credit to be utilized until expended or expired. The credit can pay for the cost of the Home Energy as well as any delivery fees or tariff charges. The Supplier agrees to provide once a year an accurate written list of FAP customers along with any remaining Benefit balance.

Section 4. NON-DISCRIMINATION AND ADVERTISING

The Supplier shall not advertise in a manner that implies that FAP assistance is available only through that Supplier, or that FAP applications are taken by the Supplier, or that in any other way misleads the public about the FAP.

The Supplier will assure that no Eligible Households will be treated adversely because of such assistance under applicable provisions of New Hampshire law. The Supplier will not discriminate in either the cost of goods or services provided against any Eligible Household whose behalf the State of New Hampshire or its agents make Payments. The Supplier also agrees to respect the confidentiality of those households participating in the Fuel Assistance Program.

Section 5. FUEL ASSISTANCE CONTRACT DURATION AND TERMINATION

The Supplier agrees to notify the Subgrantee and the NH FAP if it is not able to fulfill any or all of the requirements in this vendor agreement at any time. The Supplier’s failure to comply with any of the provisions of this Vendor Agreement shall, at the sole option of the FAP, enable the FAP to terminate this Vendor Agreement without liability thereto, and entitle the FAP to bar the Supplier from participation in future Fuel Assistance Programs administered by the State of New Hampshire and to avail itself of any other remedies available under any applicable law. The terms of this agreement and its execution are subject to the applicable laws and regulations of New Hampshire. This Vendor Agreement shall be in effect until midnight August 1, 2028. body: Appeal and Fair Administrative Hearing Procedures All Fuel Assistance Program (FAP) applicants who question their denial or the benefits provided are entitled to appeal the decision, which may include a Fair Administrative Hearing. Below is information regarding the appeal and hearing process. Any applicant has the right to appeal within 30 days of receiving the benefit determination letter for any of the following reasons: Applicant believes application was wrongly denied Applicant disagrees with the amount of the benefit awarded Applicant believes application was not processed within 60 days of application date (1) To appeal, the applicant should first contact the Community Action agency that processed the application. The FAP director will conduct a review and meet with the applicant via phone or virtual meeting or in person within 10 days of the applicant s request. At the meeting, the applicant will have an opportunity to express any concerns and the FAP Director will have an opportunity to attempt to resolve the dispute. (2) If the applicant is not satisfied with the outcome of this meeting, they will be referred to the NH Department of Energy (NH DOE) for a second review. The NH FAP Administrator will conduct a second review and meet with the applicant via phone or virtual meeting or in person within 10 days of the applicant s request. (3) If the applicant is not satisfied with the outcome after the two stages of the appeal above, the applicant may request in writing a Fair Administrative Hearing within 30 days of the conversation with the NH FAP Administrator. The hearing will be scheduled within 20 days of the written request and will meet the following standards: All hearings shall be held in a location reasonably convenient to the applicant. The hearing officer shall be a NH DOE employee who was not involved in rendering the challenged action or decision. The hearing officer shall review the applicant file prior to the hearing, including: FAP application, including supporting household and income documentation Written notification to the applicant of denial or other contested decision Notes and/or documentation containing information relied upon by FAP staff when making the decision to deny benefits or take the contested action Applicants have the right to review all documentation prior to the hearing, including the FAP Policy and Procedures Manual. Applicants can bring a representative to the hearing if they wish at their expense. Applicants can request an interpreter to be provided and funded by the NH DOE. At the hearing, applicants may present oral testimony, a written statement, or other evidence and have the right to present witnesses and cross-examine witnesses. The hearing will be recorded and the decision based on the record and any relevant evidence and information introduced during the hearing. A written decision will be issued by the NH DOE within 10 business days of the hearing.

body: Assurance 7 The State agrees, if the State chooses to pay home energy suppliers directly, to establish procedures to: (A) notify each participating household of the amount of assistance paid on its behalf; (B) assure that the home energy supplier will charge the eligible household, in the normal billing process, the difference between the actual cost of the home energy and the amount of payment made by the State under this title; (C) assure that the home energy supplier will provide assurances that any agreement entered into with a home energy supplier under this paragraph will contain provisions to assure that no household receiving assistance under this title will be treated adversely because of such assistance under applicable provisions of State law or public regulatory requirements; and (D) ensure that the provision of vendor payments remains at the option of the State in consultation with the local grantees and may be contingent upon unregulated vendors taking appropriate measures to alleviate the energy burdens of eligible households, including providing for agreements between suppliers and individuals eligible for benefits under this Act that seek to reduce home energy costs, minimize the risks of home energy crisis, and encourage regular payments by individuals receiving financial assistance for home energy costs. Assurance 8 The State agrees to provide assurances that: (A) the State will not exclude households described in clause (2)(B) of this subsection from receiving home energy assistance benefits under clause (2), and (B) the State will treat owners and renters equitably under the program assisted under this title. Assurance 9 The State agrees to provide that: (A) the State may use for planning and administering the use of funds under this title, an amount not to exceed 10 percent of the funds payable to such State under this title for a fiscal year; and (B) the State will pay from non-federal sources the remaining costs of planning and administering the program assisted under this title, and will not use federal funds for such remaining costs (except for the costs of the activities described in paragraph (16). Assurance 10 The State agrees to provide that such fiscal control and fund accounting procedures will be established as may be necessary to assure the proper disbursal of and accounting for federal funds paid to the State under this title, including procedures for monitoring the assistance provided under this title, and also provides that the State will comply with the provisions of chapter 75 of title 31, United States Code (commonly known as the "Single Audit Act").

Assurance 11 The State agrees to permit and cooperate with Federal investigations undertaken in accordance with section 2608. Assurance 12 The State agrees to provide for timely and meaningful public participation in the development of the plan described in subsection (c). Assurance 13 The State agrees to provide an opportunity for a fair administrative hearing to individuals whose claims for assistance under the plan described in subsection (c) are denied or are not acted upon with reasonable promptness.

Assurance 14 The State agrees to cooperate with the Secretary with respect to data collecting and reporting under section 2610. Assurance 15 The State agrees to (beginning in fiscal year 1992) provide, in addition to such services as may be offered by State Departments of Public Welfare at the local level, outreach and intake functions for crisis situations and heating and cooling assistance that is administered by additional State and local governmental entities or community-based organizations (such as community action agencies, area agencies on aging and not-for-profit neighborhood-based organizations), and in states where such organizations do not administer functions as of September 30, 1991, preference in awarding grants or contracts for intake services shall be provided to those agencies that administer the low-income weatherization or energy crisis intervention programs. * This assurance is applicable only to states and to territories whose annual regular LIHEAP allotments exceed $200,000. Neither territories with annual allotments of $200,000 or less nor Indian tribes/tribal organizations are subject to Assurance 15. Assurance 16 The State agrees to use up to 5 percent of such funds, at its option, to provide services that encourage and enable households to reduce their home energy needs and thereby the need for energy assistance, including needs assessments, counseling, and assistance with energy vendors, and to report to the Secretary concerning the impact of such activities on the number of households served, the level of direct benefits provided to those households, and the number of households that remain unserved.
